genericProblem: An interaction artifact can describe a valid user task while omitting the concrete shared frontend primitive that must realize its shared behavior, or while relying on a waived visual-baseline requirement without a durable waiver record.
rootCauseClass: The IA template carried user-task, surface, copy and technical-boundary declarations but did not turn the RM1 plan's per-artifact foundation binding and the visual-baseline exception into explicit screen-level admission fields.
finiteDenominator: doc/decisions/2026-07-28-v2s-rm1-ia-02-operation-context-interaction.md (13 implementation screens plus one rejected source candidate)
searchedSurfaces: the initial 24 IA01/IA02 candidate-inclusive Screen declarations; after Dexter's selector decision, 23 implementation screens plus one rejected-source record
the template's declaration, counterpart and ownership rosters
the P6 final-design admission standard and RM1 plan UI-amendment contract
the public admin-ui-foundation export barrel and current frontend architecture gate
counterexamples: A page whose only shared behavior is its test locator may bind testId; it must not invent a Drawer or query-context primitive merely to avoid NONE_WITH_REASON.
A Drawer that collects mutable form data must bind useDrawerFormLifecycle and adminDrawerSurfaceProps; a read-only Drawer must not claim that form lifecycle as a false requirement.

An implementation-file import check cannot be evaluated from a pre-implementation IA alone when no exact delivery path exists; it becomes mandatory once final P6 binds screen to actual path and must then have a real red mutation.
A Dexter-waived static counterpart is not equivalent to a missing counterpart: the waiver date, scope and alternate review evidence must be declared so a later review can distinguish the two.

findings.evidence: RM1 plan §7 lines 380-400 requires each IA amendment to bind a foundation primitive, while the template and the initial 24 candidate-inclusive IA declarations lacked a concrete admin-ui-foundation export. index.ts exports the applicable shared lifecycle, Drawer surface, overlay, query-context and automation primitives.

The current frontend gate enforces architecture-wide properties but contains no IA screen-to-implementation path manifest, so it cannot honestly prove declared-import equality at the IA stage. Final P6 must bind exact delivery paths, then add the import equality control and a local reimplementation red mutation before implementation closure.

The template requires static counterparts for EXACT/PARTIAL rows; Dexter explicitly waived drawing copied mockups for this IA review. IA02 recorded R5 anchors but not the waiver/equivalent evidence, making the exceptional admission indistinguishable from an omission.

The template allowed only PASS/REVISE while IA02 initially used REVISE_PENDING_DEXTER for the Header-versus-side-footer workspace selector source conflict. Dexter decided the side-footer on 2026-07-29; the Header candidate is now retained only as rejected-source evidence, not as a screen or pending roster row.
